newsitem.title: USA: Complacency on stock markets is dangerous--Summers.
newsitem.headline: Complacency on stock markets is dangerous--Summers.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday that it was potentially dangerous to be too complacent about stock markets or the economy as a whole.

"I get worried when I hear people say that, because it's a new era, the business cycle is over or recessions have been banished or that the stock market is now an escalator and it goes only in one direction," Summers told attendees at a conference on emerging economies.
"Those kinds of notions that point towards too much complacency can be quite dangerous," he added.
Summers also said that, at the moment, the future for the U.S. economy was very bright.
"I think the American economy, right now, (and) the American economic expansion, is extraordinarily healthy," he said.
